reviews.text: 直接主题 因为测试版刷爆（我技能点300级，第二章开启，直接点满天赋了）所以常规三章没什么难度 三章过后，游戏难度暴增，所有资源清零，7局定胜负，你可以理解为在规定的牌局内，选出你觉得可以胜出的牌，很肝！ 现在请马上更新： ·需要关闭特效设置！！！ ·Need to turn off the skill special effects settings！！！！ · スキル効果の設定をオフにする必要があります！！！

首先这是纯粹的数值游戏 我建议你开着ce玩 打完第三章会让你进终局 终局是将你所有的东西删除 只留下星座（本来也没几点）➡️星座点数大头全在终局 你所有的东西都会清零 他甚至专门给你做了套新局外成长 （原本的局外成长叫剧情局外成长） 然后 终局给你的新限制是在有限局游戏次数内通关3个章节（对就是原本的剧情，数值没有任何改变） 已知打完一把给3k魂 强满一个遗物要1w多（一玩一个不吱声） 然后本身的数值就极度不平滑 每半章就需要你更新武器 我的评价是垃圾游戏 整个玩下来就像一个借了别人的框架然后自己塞了点东西就出来骗钱的（简单抄点）

玩DEMO的时候我有多喜欢这游戏，我现在就有多想骂设计师，我以为正式版要整个大的，结果他给我拉了坨大的。 战役模式我能给60分，但这个弱智一样的升华模式我只能给10分，没买的朋友请三思。 简单解释一下，就是主线只有3章，作者为了让游戏内容看起来更丰富一些，在主线完结后可以升华，也就是转生。会清除除了星座以外的所有东西，包括屋里那口钟......然后以更高难度重新开始游戏，并且要在有限次数内打通这三章剧情，当完成挑战后会继续清空所有东西重生，然后挑战更高难度。 目前游戏的问题很多，比如： [olist] [*]游戏内容量太少：剧情模式就3章，好用的技能并不多，而这其中很多是因为没有好用的装备去配合。这种游戏就算技能一开始再难用，只要有合适的装备进行搭配，也能玩出很强的效果，但目前游戏的装备太少了。 [*]优化有问题：在法术、投射物、怪多的时候，帧数会掉的很厉害，甚至有时候所有圆形的技能特效会在画面中显示成方格状，部分贴图会鬼畜般闪烁起来。 [*]有bug，触发条件不清楚，具体效果是有概率在关卡结束返回城镇后，游戏速度变得非常慢，所有操作包括移动、攻击、放技能都跟子弹时间一样，且小退游戏后有概率无法恢复，只能大退游戏后才能解决。 [*]局外养成太漫长了，并不是说局外养成内容不能做太多，而是得有其他内容量跟着一起匹配，比如随着养成的深入，可以解锁更多装备，或者通过加点达成某些新玩法，让玩家一直有新鲜感。而不是像现在这样量大但不管饱，局外养成的内容全是什么火焰抗性+5，移速+5，爆伤+5......你搁这PDD砍一刀呢？ [*]设置功能待完善，比如初始亮度太低了，我调到最亮依旧看不清很多东西；再比如没有技能效果透明度，导致部分流派在后期的时候根本看不清路，技能效果亮的舍友以为我在学电焊。 [*]希望能添加稻草人这种可以试验伤害的东西，以方便测试BD伤害，或者能测试某些效果能不能应用到某个技能上。 [*]这个星座功能，真的有想让我点完吗，游戏体量做的这么少，星座功能做的这么大？打一章一般也就能遇到2~3次祭坛，这么大个星座图我得点到哪年去？ [*]在对局结束时，应该加入一个分解装备的功能，就像怪猎完成任务后，可以选择卖出材料一样，最后不卖的才放入仓库，而不是每次打完都把一堆垃圾塞到我仓库里，让我自己再从仓库把它们一件一件挑出来。 [*]仓库内希望能加入整理功能和筛选功能，不然东西多了整理起来真的非常烦躁，研究bd的时候也需要一件件装备反复查看信息。 [*]最恶心的还是这个新模式，这类游戏本身就是需要反复刷装备，凑bd，培养局外养成元素才能爽起来的游戏，我辛辛苦苦打了半天，打通了之后正准备优化bd开始爽呢，你就全都给我删了？想不删就只能在之前的难度下玩，想玩更高难度就得删档？作者你到底用哪个器官思考之后决定做这个功能的？ [/olist]

[h2]神钟一响，魂石万两[/h2] 游戏的节奏很快，每一局都有一个倒计时，逼着玩家不停的前进（当然也可以取消倒计时模式，这样玩的更轻松，看个人喜好），玩家可以在地牢刷怪升级，捡金币买临时的祝福，但这些都是带不走的。真正能让玩家变强的是魂石和遗物这两样局外资源，魂石可以用来在营地里永久升级技能、购买更好的装备、升级遗物，还能在神钟里点天赋，提升各种属性。而遗物就像是拼图，需要玩家把它镶嵌在一个有限的格子里，不同的遗物有不同的效果，我最喜欢玩的是“送钟流”给敌人送终，一砸一大片，带上亡者丧钟遗物，还会有猛男跟你一起作战，真的爽，什么恶毒的尸骸、什么掘行战士，跟我的古钟说去吧，我还以为减速带呢。 [h2]黑暗画风与爽快手感[/h2] 游戏的画风是黑暗奇幻风格，挺有《暗黑破坏神》的味道，打击音效做的也不错，很爽，游戏背景设定在19世纪的巴西，改编自真实的历史事件卡努杜斯战争，感兴趣的可以去了解一下。 [h2]美中不足[/h2] 有时候会有卡顿，鼠标移到某个遗物上看词条的时候，画面会突然卡一下，还有加载动画也大概率会卡一下。有些地方的汉化也还没做完，会蹦出几个英文。还有个令人困惑的地方就是你每次进地牢死了都得从开头开始打，怪物和地图都是一样的，打久了有些无聊，感觉有故意拉长游戏时间的嫌疑，还有就是终局的内容，无力吐槽了，会清空你之前辛辛苦苦打的进度，然后重新来，不过好在官方也说了“我们的终局内容仍处于测试阶段，期待与你们一同完善！”，希望后面会改进吧。 [h2]总结[/h2] 地狱丧钟是一款融合了肉鸽元素的快节奏ARPG，核心玩法就是进地牢，刷刷刷，通过收集魂石和遗物不断强化自己，战斗手感非常爽快。不过目前也存在一些优化问题，比如卡顿，再就是终局的内容目前饱受诟病，希望后续会改进。总体而言，游戏值得入手。 [quote] 恭请雅鉴 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

刚开始的一两个小时还算有意思，后面越玩越无聊，我很多把玩着玩着直接睡着了 问题在哪里？ 本质上这游戏就不是肉鸽，纯粹的刷子游戏，我认为的肉鸽是在局内通过选取不同特性构筑当局的build，最终build成型的时候获得爽感，每局随机的原因，构筑情况不同，方向不同，有成有败，但体验都会不同，但这个游戏所有与机制构筑和大部分的数值培养相关的部分都在局外，影响技能机制的遗物局内掉落但不能即时装备，要在局外提前装备好（还有格子卡构筑），影响额外机制的培养在星图里，要靠不断刷星图点去点出来，相当于技能，局内能选的只有数值，比如伤害量、技能范围、冷却时间这种的，相当于进游戏前已经限定死了这把的玩法，没有任何新鲜感，所以越玩越困越玩越没意思 更别提遗物词条随机，魂石消耗量巨大，星图点要爆肝而且通关还清空培养了，妥妥的要命

Let me preface this with the fact that I am an avid roguelike/roguelite player, and I've also played exile-like games such as PoE2 and Last Epoch. I bought this game 2 days after its release and as of writing this, I have clocked 48h of gameplay and have cleared Hell 5 with much ease. Now, this game is indeed incomplete, but I am still giving it a recommend as I'm not very hard to please. [b]Why is it incomplete?[/b] 1. They are still testing out what systems would work best for their endgame. They literally said the endgame was in Beta. I don't see this as a bad thing if the developers intend to make it the best game that they can (I hope they do). 2. Very inbalanced scaling for boss health and damage. Some find this a turnoff, I see it as a challenge. But I do see why many people can struggle with this if they're new to either roguelike/roguelite and/or exile-like genres. Also feel like some skills/relics are much more potent than others. [spoiler]Looking at you bombardment, the CD reduction per hit just destroys any other builds by far IMO, not complaining tho ;)[/spoiler] 3. Lack of clarity for ALOT of things. I had to do alot of testing in-game. These are a few off the top of my head. - There is a relic that gives stacking melee dmg upon "Lifesteal". There is only one other gear (one of the rings) I've seen that uses the same term, "Lifesteal". I've tested this with multiple other relics with effects I think may be counted as "Lifesteal". The double knives relic that converts dmg to life -> counted as Lifesteal. Life on Kill -> counted as Lifesteal. The kicker, however, is that you have to have missing health in order for you to proc Lifesteal to provide the stacking melee dmg buff. - Global buffs per skill rank. Didn't take long for me to notice that increasing the skill rank didn't give the global buffs, But only realised before writing this review that what that meant is that for whatever skill you bring into the run, you get those buffs per level added into that skill. - Initially had no idea what some of the statuses did (looking at shocked and blight). My presumption was shocked contributed to stun and blight amplified damage taken, but that's not what it did. They have since added tooltips when you hover over the stats in the character sheet in the 1.0.1 update, so alls good. - I would think double knives and reflexes count as AoE skills since they are literally AoE and their AoE can be increased via leveling up. However, they do not have the AoE tag. So does increased AoE damage not apply to these skills? I have not tested this. - I wasn't sure where my base damage numbers were coming from. Increasing base damage by 50 gave me more than 50 base damage when reflected in the character sheet. Not sure if that's a bug or are there some other hidden multipliers. If so, would be good for devs to include a tooltip to show damage calculations (and likewise for other stats such as crit, status chance etc.). - Pretty sure I saw something somewhere mentioning "Toxic" instead of "Plague", not a big issue tho. - For leveling up effects related to relics (eg. explosion area for the quill relic, activation speed for book of sin for judgement), apparently they can be allocated to any skill, not just the skill that the relic affects. Not sure if this is a bug or if it's intended. Also not sure if it's only some or all relics. 4. Plenty of QoL missing. I will mention this further in a suggestions section below. [b]Pros[/b] 1. Tons of damage, its just nice to see damage numbers in the hundred thousands and occasionally millions. 2. Build variety. Even with these 20+ or so skills, I feel like there's currently enough relics and skills for me to test multiple builds to see what works and how to improve on them. 3. Simple gameplay loop. Do a run, get soulstones/constellation points. Improve passive skill/constellation tree. Some prefer a more complicated loop, I think its great for beginners of the genre. 4. Relaxed mode. Again, good for beginners. They have also included Vengeance mode in 1.0.1. 5. Thank god for red gates. I also didn't know they only added the exp and gold buff in 1.0.1. I thought it was in the game on release. 6. All the loot flies to you if you kill every single mob in a map. I feel like this was only added in 1.0.1 but I didn't see it anywhere in their patch notes. You still have to kill every single mob tho. But there is a constellation somewhere that lets items get global-sucked when you kill a rare mob. [b]Cons[/b] Apart from the reasons why the game feels incomplete: 1. WHERE IS THE SORT/SEARCH FOR RELICS JESUS. Would also be good to include search function in the passive tree if devs intend to expand the tree further. 2. Constellation tree reset, at least for the campaign. I understand that in the endgame mode, we have to allocate points dynamically based on what build we're trying to go for and what relics the runs give us so that's fine. But its extremely important for build testing when returning to the campaign. Devs did mention that they're working on this. 3. A few but important bugs that need fixing. - Game suddenly going super slow when returning from a run, I've experienced this twice and I didn't know what was causing it. It's since been fixed in 1.0.1. - Constellation points missing in hell mode. After finishing Hell 5 and returning to campaign, I had 27 points. When I entered Hell 10, I only had 21. Not sure if this is intended, could it be that you're given a set amount of points at the beginning of each new hell level? Pretty sure I was supposed to carry forward all my constellation points though, or am I mistaken? - Devotion path completion not giving me the completion points as intended (GAME BREAKING). I'm pretty sure this is a bug. I've encountered it twice where I maxed out a constellation and it did not give me the completion points. One of this was in my first hell mode run, Hell 2. This I could handle, since the world can be resetted. But the other one is in my campaign mode and it's crippling my gameplay experience. Might not continue until this is fixed (without me having to start a new save file). PSA. I think this happens when you have enough points to max out more than 1 constellation in 1 go when allocating new constellation points. - Act 2 boss (14F) can sometimes freeze/get stuck while in the air because he has a jumping/dive AoE move, and you can't damage him while hes up there. Currently couldn't find a way to get him back down as far as I know, forcing a rerun. 4. Repetitive. Not a big con for me for now but I think it will get boring after awhile. I've almost memorised the layout for all the maps. Devs did mention that they intend to include more acts/variety of maps in the future. [b]Suggestions[/b] 1. Relic sort/search as mentioned, definitely please include this. Devs did mention that they are working on it. 2. Allow renaming of relic pages, and drag and drop relic pages to re-order them. 3. Save button. I'm not sure when exactly does the game auto-saves. I've quitted the game after making changes to my build and before entering a new run and it was saved. But at the same time, I assumed it was after each completed run of an Act because the gear shop resets everytime I reload, so that doesn't get saved and allows us to bypass the redraw cost (although its not that expensive). So I'm not sure which one is intended and which one isn't. 4. Game manual/FAQ, devs are already working on it. 5. Mentioned above, but tooltips for how each stat is calculated would be good. 6. Transparency slider for damage numbers. I still want to see big damage numbers but I don't want it to completely cover my screen such that I can't see what's going on. 7. Standardisation of terms used (see example on "Lifesteal" above) 8. PLEASEEEE let me move while casting the quill spell instead of stopping each time i cast it (might be intended this way but man would it be good if i didn't have to stop every 0.25s)

看游戏的玩法以及画面，《地狱丧钟》都很很容易让人联想到同为肉鸽动作爽游《哈迪斯》，但老实说其核心体验却又稍有些不同，虽然肉鸽这一玩法可结合的元素有很多，但《地狱丧钟》在肉鸽构筑的基础上把类暗黑的刷子玩法结合的玩法还真不太多见，二者产生的化学反应在实际游玩体验上也确实不错，aoe为主的各种流派技能在局内也确实带来无限的割草爽感！ [h1]当肉鸽遇上刷宝[/h1] 这游戏还是取材一个真实的战争背景的，19世纪末巴西腹地的卡努杜斯，一场共和军对平民聚落的血腥镇压夺走了25000条生命，制作组则是通过黑暗幻想的手法将其描绘，主角每一次深入地狱的目的是打破无尽的轮回，拯救自己导师的灵魂，每一次轮回既是战斗，也是对历史的修正！ 游戏的核心玩法框架其实是比较简单的，在七分钟有限的时间内深入地狱，击杀敌人、收集战利品并尽可能地通往更深层地关卡，时间归零即强制遣返地面。和大多数肉鸽游戏一样游戏主要分为局内和局外的构筑，通过属性的构筑叠加来完成单局的不同体验，但就本作来说，它更多的是以局外成长为主导，局内的构筑主要围绕开局前所携带的技能而获取一些额外的技能效果以及以及击杀怪物随机获取的局内可用的装备，更多的都是一些基础属性的提升。 掉落的魂石、遗物等强化内容都需要在局外使用，你这一局的价值永远在于为下一局铺路，所以局内玩家并没有太多的决策空间，但老实说局内游戏体验也因为装备掉落驱动并且在构筑成形后绞肉机般的割草玩法爽感一直在线，各种技能都很流畅打击感十足！ 游戏局外的构筑则比较丰富，依靠局内掉落的魂石可以解锁不同的技能、天赋，局内掉落的遗物则是不同流派构筑的主要内容，也可以通过魂石来升级。游戏局内虽然有着装备掉落这一类暗黑玩法驱动，但本质上并不算一款比较肝的游戏，虽然一些好的遗物需要多次刷取，但属性提升后前面的小怪基本就是无脑切菜，它更多的是依赖不同流派成型的数值来驱动，局内阶段性的小boss战关卡结束后下一层敌人会迎来数值上的暴涨，也就迫使你多回到营地去研究流派构筑！ [h1]写在后面[/h1] 游戏目前为ea阶段，体量并不算大，局内的肉鸽的元素并不算很强，，但肉鸽和类暗黑的刷子玩法结合体验也确实不错，遗物系统构筑出深邃的BD流派，通过数值爬升能带来持续的满足感，局外成长的确定性反而成为了优点。 [quote=][b]评测出自：[u]网易 UU 鉴赏家培训计划[/u][/b] [b]感谢由[u]网易 UU 鉴赏家培训计划[/u]提供游戏[/b] [i][b]加速云存领游戏，满足热爱游戏梦！[/b][/i][/quote]

[h1]丧钟为谁而鸣？ [/h1] 《地狱丧钟》是一款暗黑刷宝类肉鸽佳作。本作的玩法更接近暗黑破坏神这类刷宝游戏，肉鸽元素并不多，主要存在于装备词条和升级技能中。游戏最大的特色是在每一局的准备阶段换上不同的技能在爬塔过程中强化构筑流派。看到自己不断尝试与技能有关的核心遗物和技能打出爆炸的伤害，很容易享受到角色成长的乐趣。 [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [b][u][i]U_U鉴赏家培养计划[/i][/u][/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注U_U鉴赏家，开启精彩游戏之旅。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] [h2]游戏背景 [/h2] 本作取材于真实历史中发生的卡努图斯大屠杀事件，这次我们要扮演的是一名时钟使者，去地牢拯救被抓住的同伴，狠狠地惩罚那些入侵我们国家的敌人。游戏一共有三幕，通关后可以解锁升华地狱，来挑战更多的层数。 [h2]基本玩法 [/h2] 每次下地牢的时间有限，玩家需要尽可能通往最高的楼层，其中BOSS房不消耗时间。主线任务是一个BOSS一个任务，前几次打不到也不用急，因为有技能没点出来，等解锁了天赋树之后，会有个传送门的技能，可以直接跳过一关，非常方便，这个机制也是玩家能打到20多层的关键。在游玩的过程中，我们会遇到宝箱，随机掉落护符；升级后在三个技能里三选一，没有想要的可以花钱重ROLL，每个技能只有一个史诗加成，建议留给需要的方向。 （不过一般都是伤害）此外升级后出现的技能选择和我们搭配的技能有关，那么如果想玩一两个核心技能的流派，建议只带这几个技能，这样有把握每次都能刷到与之相关的技能，成长起来也更快。 [h2]局外成长[/h2] 每一局游戏都会获得一定数量的魂晶，拿出来后，可以用来学习新技能，升级遗物品级，点天赋树以及购买装备。天赋树有很多非常实用的技能，比如之前提到的传送门就是其中之一，其他还有增加金币获取、灵魂获取等能力，都能让玩家更快的积累财富。 技能方面是和遗物搭配的，每个遗物都会强化某一种技能，有些特别有用，有些强化了也不好用，不想要的遗物可以用来分解成魂晶。比如最开始的普通技能带有燃烧效果的“分裂射击”，看似普普通通，到第三幕通过遗物和技能加成方面的叠加，甚至可以打出上亿的伤害。另外遗物也有品阶和星级之分，越到后门的楼层获取，遗物的质量也就越高。 出来后还可以在若昂处购买装备，这个装备的效果不是叠加的，而是购买后新的装备会顶掉旧装备，所以购买之前要比对数值。 [h2]升华 [/h2] 主线三幕剧情打通后，可以在石碑附近借宿星域图这种东西，玩过《恐怖黎明》的应该都懂，需要根据玩家的流派进行星座技能选择。升华就是更高的难度，一般都是为了给自己增加一点挑战性的玩家会去游玩。 [h2]总结 [/h2] 《地狱丧钟》的玩法极其有趣，技能数量众多，可以做成很多流派的构筑，这种有趣的暗黑耍宝玩法是我为数不多感觉爽的了。特别是好多BOSS一开始需要花尽心思打败他们，但随着角色的升级和新的技能点出来后，基本几秒就能解决这层的BOSS，这种累积爽的玩法，真的非常推荐刷宝爱好者游玩本作！

[h1]这竟然是一款快节奏动作肉鸽刷子ARPG[/h1] 《地狱丧钟 Hell Clock》是一款基于巴西真实历史事件“卡努杜斯大屠杀”改编的快节奏动作肉鸽刷子ARPG，游戏里我们将操作一名名为帕杰乌的反抗军战士，为了拯救卡努杜斯的精神领袖顾问的灵魂，在卡努杜斯大钟能量的帮助下，不断的穿越时间、扭曲时间，进入被地狱时钟扭曲的地狱时空里，与那些操纵黑暗势力、夺走顾问首级并囚禁其灵魂的恶魔不停的战斗。 [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [b][u][i]U_U鉴赏家培养计划[/i][/u][/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注U_U鉴赏家，开启精彩游戏之旅。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] [h1]虽说剧情改编自真实历史，但玩这类游戏谁又会在意呢！？[/h1] 如同前面所说，《地狱丧钟 Hell Clock》是有剧情推动的，虽说在剧情的描写上还是较为单薄，但各种漫画形式的过场和平时NPC之间的只言片语也足够让我们对整个剧情有所了解。而且话又说回来了，这么一款有着暗黑风格的动作肉鸽刷刷刷游戏，谁又会那么在意剧情说什么呢？！ [h1]游戏逼着我们做选择，还能逼得我们身爽！[/h1] 《地狱丧钟 Hell Clock》的另一个特色是它既有着《流放之路》的深度BD系统，又有着《哈迪斯》的动作肉鸽快感，还有着由“地狱时钟”倒数给予我们的时间紧迫感。这些个特色融合之下，很能让我们这些平时玩刷刷刷游戏，喜欢悠闲的四处乱逛多探索一些“好处”的玩家们，增加不少新鲜感！是急忙赶路？还是多探索一些地方？还是多杀一些怪物提升等级？在这里每一局的新开始都在逼着我们不停的做选择，相当有意思。 [h1]在时间倒数中不断的变强！[/h1] 每次进入地狱深渊时空里，那寥寥几分钟的地狱时钟就会开始倒数（之后可以使用魂石在“卡努杜斯大钟”解锁并激活天赋树选项来延长时间）。我们就需要在这有限的时间里，不断的深入地狱深渊，击杀更多的恶魔军团来获取各种“远古圣物”，并将不同的“远古圣物”组合成战斗流派核心，构筑更强的战斗流派来让我们在地狱深渊里走得更远更深。 [h1]爽快的战斗、有意思的技能加强！[/h1] 游戏的战斗手感相当不错，别看我们的主角手头似乎就一把看着火力不怎么充足的小手铳就小看他了，这丫的成长起来可不把恶魔们当一回事！在战斗过程中升级能获得各种技能加强，不过这里的在选择上又有了新花样！我们在其他肉鸽游戏里做选择的时候当然往高级了选，但在《地狱丧钟 Hell Clock》这里每个技能能接受的加强等阶数量是有数量限制的，每个技能只能接受一次史诗加强+2次稀有加强+3次魔法加强+4次普通加强，因此在选择的时候一定要认真思考，别看高级就选了，不然影响BD构筑可是绝对的得不偿失！ [h1]把圣物选择玩出背包管理的味道[/h1] 各种“远古圣物”除了能给角色提供属性加成之外，还能改变技能形态，这是游戏最为核心的机制。这里极力推荐“天怒”和“侦骑勋章”！再加上几个减蓝耗和回蓝的圣物，完全可以做到让我们一路转圈圈不停歇！挑选我们游戏过程中获得的更好的“远古圣物”进圣物槽里，也是我们构筑BD的核心关键，当然，要想有更多的构筑选择，当然还是把扩充圣物槽作为第一要务是最为明智的选择！ [h1]聊胜于无的装备系统[/h1] 游戏还有这RPG游戏一般的装备系统，虽说我们战斗过程中能获得的装备较为稀少，但不打紧，在我们每次复活会基地整顿的时候，都可以使用魂石购买更好的装备，不过装备并没有什么更好的扩充，算是一个聊胜于无的提升手段吧！ [h1]DZYY了？选它！[/h1] 整体而言，《地狱丧钟 Hell Clock》这款游戏就是那种能让我们一爽再爽，越战越强根本停不下来的快节奏动作肉鸽刷刷刷游戏！如果最近玩游戏感觉没什么动力，选它准没错！绝对能治愈你的DZYY！！！

[h1]A Very Good, Highly Immoral Game[/h1] As a game, Hell Clock is great. Besides the "unusual" theme (for non-Brazilians), two particular aspects of it shine above all others: 1 - That it is a perfect blend of roguelike and ARPG. It really [i]feels[/i] like playing an ARPG, while having all the hallmarks of a roguelike (meta progression, random in-run abilities and blessings, etc.); 2 - And that, unlike in most roguelikes, [i]most[/i] of your progress is permanent. You don't just unlock more meta passive skills and bonuses, but you also get to permanently keep all of your Gear (equipped body items) and Relics (the items that [i]really[/i] affect gameplay, defining your build). I think the permanent Gear and Relics idea was great. It makes things feel a lot more rewarding, because you don't lose the most important stuff you grab during a good run. I expect to see many roguelikes copying (and hopefully expanding upon) this initiative in the future. On top of Gear, Relics, the passive-skill tree, etc., there are also Constellations in the game, which grant further passive bonuses that deeply affect gameplay, making your character considerably more powerful. Truth be told, said Constellations are a pretty direct copy of Grim Dawn's. But they are a beloved aspect of that [also great] game, something I'd like to see more often, and something I believe everyone will enjoy. [b]In short[/b], I'd say I probably had a better time playing this than Hades, which is pretty much [i]the[/i] point of reference in the genre. (Though I haven't played Hades [i]2[/i] yet.) A really good job from these Brazilian developers, and I'm glad to see there's someone left with brains in this self-destructing, God-forsaken country. Alas, Hell Clock has one big issue, which is why I called it a "[b]highly immoral game[/b]" in the title: those portrayed as victims and heroes in the game were actually zealots and criminals that, in most part, deserved to be slaughtered (excluding women, children, and the elderly [unless these were actual combatants, which they may or may not have been]). Trying to put it briefly, what happened in Canudos was that a zealot called Antônio Conselheiro decided to create a village in some private, albeit abandoned and legally-disputed, lands to spread the Catholic Church's word and encourage the dissolution of the Brazilian then newly-born Republic, defending the return of the monarchy and, on top of it, that this one should be bound by the Church's laws. In other words, he wanted to take down the Republic and instate a Catholic Monarchy in Brazil -- a regime that would completely ignore reason, abide by the Church's will and force the Catholic creed upon the population. At the time, much of the region's people were poor, miserable and, according to themselves, downtrodden. That mostly remains true to this day, not because someone screwed them, but because they settled in an arid, lifeless place and never managed to make anything good out of it. Still, at the time, that led to about 25,000 people joining Canudos, and thus Conselheiro's cause. A black spot was created. And a rumor soon started that those people intended to try to take down the Republic. The army sent a small detachment of men (100-200) to deal with the situation. These were received by armed people from Canudos, who ambushed and began to encircle them. Realizing they were about to be tactically screwed, the soldiers opened fire. And they were slaughtered. Two more incursions were sent afterward by the army, and both were defeated as well. On the fourth time, a serious contingent of troops was dispatched, and this one finally succeeded at massacring the Canudos' rebels. So, what actually happened was that a religious fanatic who the evidence suggests intended to stage a coup d'etat formed an enclave that refused to pay taxes and abide by Brazil's laws, and then created a 25,000-strong army that was clearly heavily armed and, thus, ill-intentioned. The man and his followers were [i]criminals[/i], they had to be dealt with, and they were. No one should ever praise those people and their actions. That's like praising Israel for stealing the Palestinians' lands and then doing what it has been doing to the Palestinian people for the past 80 years, more recently and starkly in Gaza. Those people -- Canudenses and Israelis -- were/are not victims. They were/are ciminals/terrorists. And portraying them as the first is a dire disservice to mankind. This is not something to be condoned. Finally, and just to be even more "inappropriately" political, Hell Clock was financed by public money. And due to the current Brazilian political scenario, there's a good chance that they wouldn't be granted that money [i]unless[/i] they portrayed the people of Canudos as victims. At the same time, it's safe to say it's [i]guaranteed[/i] they would have [i]not[/i] been granted it if the developers portrayed those people as the traitors and criminals they actually were. So it's hard to say if the developers of Hell Clock actually believe in the game's misguided morality, or if they were forced to pretend they do. Make of that what you will. [b]EDIT:[/b] Two more caveats: 1 - The last Campaign world difficulty -- Void -- is pointles. It makes everything a lot harder while not yielding [i]any[/i] reward; 2 - There's an achievement that requires you to talk to all spirits in Act III's subway station. I did that, and I didn't get the achievement. So, if you are unlucky, you won't be able to 100% the game.

I wish there was a neutral rating, and this would be a perfect game for that. I don't get all of the reviews saying it's like Diablo 3. Sure, there are some things that gave inspiration to the game, but that's about as far as it goes. For instance, there's an achievement that's called, "Stay a While and Listen" where you need to talk to all of the spirits, there's shrines, there "loot" (more on this in a second), and there's a loot goblin you will see. Sounds awesome, but it's lackluster. The "loot"... yeah, there's gear in the game, but not in the same sense as in Diablo. You will find gear, but they're all similar most of the time. For instance, you will find a Hat I, a Hat II, a hat IV, etc. Each level, most of the time, just increases the base stat. So you may have "All Resistances +2" for a Hat I, then a Hat IV may have "All Resistances +8" as an example. It's very shallow. It was fun at the beginning, but it lost it's fun really quick. On the first few acts you can blaze through those with little resistance. When you get to the final "act" it feels like the difficulty is artificially ramped up, for no reason. I would go through the first 15 floors with no issue, then on floor 16 the enemy health just spikes to where they become bullet sponges. On my last run I had so much mana regen, life leech, etc. that I could essentially just spam the one skill. I literally just stood there tanking the enemy, It would take a good minute (no joke) to take down an enemy that went down in a few seconds on the previous floor. So the reviews saying the balance is wrong, is spot on. Also, the potions are worthless in this game. You take a potion and it only refills like 2/8th of your health, if you're lucky. You start with three potions and on a boss it's not uncommon to pop them all at once, when you're like at 1/4 health. When you pop all three you get to like 3/4 health. Also, a lot of mechanics are not explained, at all. You just have to kind of figure out what does what by playing around. There are also a lot of glitches, bugs, etc. None of them are really game breaking, but they are annoying. I see what they were going for and their inspiration, but you can see it must be the developers’ first game or something. This game is not worth the full price, at all. I would say $9.99 would be a good price, but no more. With a lot of polish, a rebalance, etc. it may be worth $14.99, maybe. One final note, if you are an achievement hunter and like to 100% games, forget about it. There are some achievements that are there to purposely make you grind, for a very long time. I do not even want to finish the final act, let alone replay the game. There is no enjoyment after the 10-hour mark.

After you get stronger, despite you have to start a run from floor, it will be much smoother as you can just breeze them through at rapid pace. The game completely changed once you reached in endgame hub with option either redo campaign in harder difficulty or play in endless nightmare. With meta progression and constellation system, you can do crazy build. Run feel fast, that I could clear in 5 minutes with tons of loots. Sadly each run felt way too repetitive and samey. Since your progression are done in town, run became simple treadmill either you kill fast, you die fast or you lost because your dmg is terrible and boss stack alot of curse on you. Blessing system from survivor-like game seem fun, but not when you get like 40 popup in 5 minutes run. It doesnt give dopamine rush RNGod luck either. Biggest gripe is layout / level design that games is so fond of corridors or small hallways. Which lead to reason why I stopped playing : graphic spam. When you combine incremental with ARPG, you get system that allow you do alot of crazy things, but at cost visual clarity. You wont able to see the enemies' ground AoE or projectiles. ARPG - The loot is boring and barely has any difference in stats. There's no real character customisation so you basically end up with a different coloured hat or jacket depending on the tier of gear you equip. The skills are the same ones you've seen in 100 other ARPGs. Skill upgrades are +X% damage/area/cooldown, so it's just a case of stacking whatever stat your build relies upon most. Roguelite - There's not enough randomness between runs. Maps have the same layout, same enemy types, "elites" spawn in the same area every run. Bosses are the same every run. You need 1 resource to unlock every type of upgrade so you're best off rushing +% soul gem gain ASAP. There are 3 short acts, separated into 3 zones with 7 floors (so 21 floors per act). Hardly any variation between floors, sometimes you'll get one where it's 3 waves of enemies but 90% of the time it's just "kill everything and rush to the exit". It's lacking the seasonal mechanics/randomness of games like Path of Exile or Diablo. It literally feels like running the same 9 PoE maps on repeat (minus the fun league mechanics). Acts 1 and 2 are great design-wise, but Act 3 jumps forward to present day and feels really out of place. --- Basically it's lacking in content and direction, and feels like it should still be in Early Access. It's alright. - The game has a unique visual style that (combined with some odd UI choices) causes legibility issues sometimes, but is otherwise striking and capable of setting an oppressive tone. - The items / passives you choose for your build feel impactful, but narrow in their scope and interactions, so once you pick "Build X" your subsequent choices are basically made for you and all else falls to the wayside. - Outside of "beeline" upgrades like increased meta-currency rates or inventory space, a majority of your upgrades feel boring, unimpactful, or uninspired (like 5% resistance to a specific element). There are multiple meta-progression systems that feel incongruous with each other, tonally and / or mechanically, but do offer a feeling of progression between multiple playthroughs if you so choose. - The titular hellclock doesn't add much to the experience. Sometimes you feel frustrated that you've run out of time (possibly due to bad luck with +30 second item drops) and have to end a run prematurely, but oftentimes I'd forget it existed, with runs either ending from boss encounters or narrative stops. On paper, it's a clever idea for preventing overpowered runs from going further than intended, and it hypothetically keeps you engaged and focused on efficiency, but in practice it's either annoying or forgettable. - The narrative focus on Brazil's Massacre of Canudos is novel, if not a bit dark, but the game kinda drops you into the story without much explanation, and by the end I felt like I only had the bullet points to work from. There are times when characters, enemies, or settings will be introduced that will lack impact without the background knowledge of Canudos - which Hellclock does not always provide. - The campaign is decent and enjoyably short. Your mileage may vary depending on your skill level though, as the levels all contain the same exact layouts and content, so if you get "stuck" in your progression, the repetition can become intense. This also means that any "new game+" / "Ascension" runs you do will become increasingly dire, which is at odds with how desperately the game wants you to play through multiple subsequent runs. I don't think Hellclock is good enough to warrant the 200 hours of repeated playthroughs it wants from you, but I do think it's worth playing through the 8-ish hour campaign once, for those already curious.

This game has an interesting concept, but the balance often makes it more annoying than fun. For me the gameplay is enjoyable occasionally, but not consistently. That's why I have mixed feelings about it. The gameplay loop goes something like this: you run through floor after floor, gunning down everything in your path. The first 10–15 floors can feel almost like a formality, and then suddenly you encounter an enemy or boss with an absurd amount of health and damage. You either get destroyed, or you kill the boss only to run out of time shortly afterwards and die anyway. At times it almost feels like the game is saying, "You've made enough progress, please stop". Then you go back, upgrade your character and repeat essentially the same sequence again. The problem is that the earlier parts of each run don't feel particularly interesting after you've seen them a few times. There isn't enough enemy or level variety to make repeating the same floors feel rewarding, so the game starts to feel like you're simply running through the same hallways over and over until you eventually become strong enough to overcome the next difficulty spike. The game also has a tendency to stop your progress for reasons that don't always feel connected to your performance. For example, I managed to get through the first act by eventually becoming strong enough to cut through most enemies with ease, only to discover that I was missing a key needed to open a gate in the second act and had to backtrack again. It often feels like there's always some reason to return to previously explored areas, even when you're clearly strong enough to continue. This makes the progression feel more restrictive than genuinely challenging. There are also moments where the game forces you into awkward situations. I died in one Nightmare Portal because an enemy regenerated health almost as quickly as my repeater could deal damage. The only realistic option was to stand close and spam attacks as fast as possible, which made it easy to lose track of my own health and die. Encounters like this feel less like a test of skill and more like a test of whether your build can outscale the enemy's mechanics. The progression systems do become much more enjoyable after the first few hours. I think the skill and upgrade systems generally respect the player's time, and the upgrades feel more meaningful than in many other dungeon crawlers or roguelikes. I found that investing skill points into useful abilities and recycling equipment to afford relic upgrades had a much bigger impact on my progress than simply finding stronger weapons or optimizing my skill set. Once I started focusing on relics that matched my playstyle and upgrading them consistently, the game became noticeably more enjoyable. I also noticed that the equipment available improved significantly in Act 2. Despite its flaws, the game does have a satisfying sense of progression. Runs don't always play out exactly the same, and it's easy to notice how much stronger your character becomes if you consistently invest in skills, relics and equipment. The upgrade systems are honestly one of the strongest parts of the game, although the overall progression can still feel like a bit of a grind. But some of the game's skills and systems don't always behave as consistently as I would expect. For example, I used a skill called Phantom Marksmen that is supposed to summon rifles to help me in combat. The skill consumes mana, so I naturally expected the rifles to appear and contribute damage. But in some boss fights the rifles simply didn't appear at all or spawned outside the map. I couldn't tell whether this was an intentional restriction or a bug. It's particularly frustrating because boss fights are exactly where I would expect additional sources of damage to be most useful. When a skill you have invested in and spent mana on simply doesn't work in certain encounters without any explanation, it makes the already complicated progression systems feel even more inconsistent. Act 2 felt noticeably easier than the first act, which made the overall difficulty curve feel inconsistent. After struggling with several brutal difficulty spikes early on, I was surprised by how much more manageable the enemies became later. However, Acts 2 and 3 also turned into a matter of waiting for a DPS increase. Even after turning my repeater into a machine gun with endlessly regenerating mana, the Minister of War could still tank more damage than I was capable of dealing during my first runs. This pattern repeated with each boss fight. Either you can't deal enough damage or you die due to lack of resistances. Bosses have large health bars in many roguelike games, but in this game it sometimes feels like you're literally fighting the health bar itself. I also agree with many other reviewers that the Hell Clock timer often makes the gameplay worse instead of more exciting. It frequently ends your run before it feels like you've reached the most interesting part. Red portals that let the player skip floors also seem to exist because even the developers know that repeating 20-something floors before getting another chance to fight a boss will eventually tire many players. I'm not even sure if it's possible to complete all the floors in the later parts of the game without using them or investing heavily in speed upgrades. Would I recommend this game? Probably not. While Hell Clock has enjoyable combat, responsive controls, excellent visuals and a surprisingly satisfying progression system, I don't think they're enough to compensate for the repetitive runs, inconsistent difficulty and the many mechanics that artificially interrupt your progress. There are many systems, like conviction, that are not explained to the player until you start putting skill points to it. Many boss fights are just standstills where both are shooting at each other, unable to kill the other. So you just spend like 10 minutes doing nothing but shooting the boss for absolutely no reason or finish the run prematurely like you should. There's a good game underneath, but I spent too much time feeling like the game was preventing me from having fun.
